name: Tamar Matossian
title: Neurodevelopmental Specialist
photoAlt: Tamar Matossian, founder and director of The Hummingbird Nest
bio:
Tamar is a Neurodevelopmental Specialist who specializes in the DIR Floortime® approach, with {years} years of experience working with the neurodiverse population. She is the founder and director of The Hummingbird Nest and the author of the book [What’s Autism](https://www.amazon.com/dp/069285620X).

Tamar holds a CL1 Profectum Certification for DIR Floortime®, a Speech Language Pathology Assistant License, and UCLA PEERS® Certification for [The Social Club](https://www.thesocialclubkids.com) social learning group program. She uses a multidisciplinary approach in all of her sessions to support maximum development.

Tamar also leads staff trainings for schools and child care facilities and provides parent coaching services.

name: Juliana Reyes
photoAlt: Juliana Reyes, DIR Floortime developmental specialist
bio:
Juliana’s approach as a DIR Floortime® Developmental Specialist at The Hummingbird Nest is grounded in relationship based, developmental, and play focused strategies. Her work emphasizes sensory regulation, body awareness, and bottom up nervous system support as the foundation for engagement and learning.

Drawing from her background as a Registered Yoga Teacher, Juliana brings movement and coregulation strategies into DIR Floortime® and Social Club sessions to help children feel safe and regulated in their bodies. She has guided children toward emotional regulation, social engagement, and meaningful connection by meeting each child at their developmental level and building trusting relationships with families.

Juliana is a graduate of the University of California, Santa Cruz, where she earned her bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Latin American and Latino Studies.

name: Selena Santana
photoAlt: Selena Santana, DIR Floortime developmental specialist
bio:
Selena Santana is a DIR Floortime® Developmental Specialist at The Hummingbird Nest with a background in psychology and cognitive science, as well as experience supporting children with autism. Her approach is rooted in relationship based, developmental, and play centered principles that put connection first as the foundation for growth.

Selena focuses on supporting social development and independence in daily routines, helping children build the skills they need for meaningful participation in everyday life. She brings sensory awareness and coregulation strategies into her sessions to promote engagement, flexibility, and confidence. By following each child’s lead and honoring their individual developmental profile, Selena fosters authentic connection while partnering closely with families to support ongoing progress.
